tips: Plant the bulb with the top half above the substrate.
Use root tabs.
Trim old leaves from the base and give it room.

items.name: Cryptocoryne Lutea
items.note: A sturdy cryptocoryne with ruffled green leaves that holds up well in many tanks. It melts when moved, then regrows from the roots.
tips: Leave it undisturbed after planting.
Use root tabs for steady growth.
Expect leaf loss after any big change.

items.name: Banana Plant (Nymphoides aquatica)
items.note: A lily-like plant with small, banana-shaped roots at the base and heart-shaped leaves that float or grow below the surface. Plant the root cluster in the substrate and leave the tops free.
tips: Do not bury the banana-shaped roots completely.
Trim floating leaves if they shade other plants.
Use root tabs for steady growth.

items.name: Glossostigma
items.note: A low carpet plant with tiny paddle-shaped leaves. It forms a dense lawn under strong light with CO2 and a fine substrate, and struggles in dim or low-nutrient tanks.
tips: Needs strong light and CO2 to stay low and dense.
Plant tiny portions spread apart.
Trim regularly so the lower layer does not die back.

items.name: Cardinal Flower (Lobelia cardinalis)
items.note: A bright green stem plant with toothed leaves that prefers cooler tanks. It is a marginal plant that grows well submerged in many aquariums, and it flowers only when it grows out of the water.
tips: Prefers cooler water than most tropical plants.
Trim tops and replant them.
Give it good light and a nutrient-rich substrate.

items.name: Mermaid Weed (Proserpinaca palustris)
items.note: A feathery stem plant with serrated leaves that turn reddish-bronze under bright light. It is easy to trim and replant and does best with good light and regular feeding.
tips: Use brighter light for stronger color.
Trim and replant tops often.
Keep nutrients steady to avoid bare lower stems.

items.name: Japanese Cress (Cardamine lyrata)
items.note: A bright green plant with rounded leaves that grows best in cooler water. In a warm tropical tank it can melt, so it suits cooler setups or tanks kept at the low end of the range.
tips: Best in cooler water; heat can make it melt.
Give it good light and nutrients.
Trim and replant healthy tops.

items.name: Lake Cress (Rorippa aquatica)
items.note: A tall stem plant with deeply cut leaves, native to cool North American waters. It grows well in cooler aquariums with good light and regular trimming, and may struggle in very warm tanks.
tips: Prefers cooler tanks.
Trim and replant tops to keep it full.
Keep nutrients steady.

items.name: Clasping-Leaf Pondweed
items.note: A tall stem plant with wavy, heart-shaped leaves that clasp the stem. It likes cooler water and hard, alkaline conditions, so it suits temperate or unheated tanks better than warm tropical ones.
tips: Best in cooler tanks.
Trim to control height.
It tolerates hard water well.

items.name: Blyxa Japonica
items.note: A rosette plant with long, grass-like leaves that forms dense, fluffy clumps. It prefers soft, slightly acidic water, CO2 and good light, and does not like to be disturbed once planted.
tips: Plant the crown above the substrate.
Does best in soft water with CO2.
Do not move it once settled.

items.name: Purple Waffle (Hemigraphis exotica)
items.note: A plant with crinkled, purple-green leaves that is often sold grown above water. It can be grown fully submerged, but the first leaves may melt before new underwater growth appears.
tips: Expect some leaf loss at first when it is moved underwater.
Needs good light for color.
Trim and replant healthy tops.

items.name: Salvini Cichlid
items.origin: Southern Mexico to Guatemala and Belize, Central America
items.diet: Carnivore: cichlid pellets, frozen foods, live foods
items.note: A bold yellow, red and black Central American cichlid. It is a strong, feisty fish that defends caves and will bully or eat smaller tankmates, so give it a roomy tank and sturdy neighbors.
tips: Use a tank of 75 gallons or more with caves and rockwork.
Do not mix with small or timid fish.
Keep the lid secure and the filtration strong.

items.name: Peacock Eel
items.temperament: Peaceful with fish too big to swallow
items.diet: Carnivore: live and frozen worms, shrimp, sinking foods
items.note: A slim, eel-like fish with a row of eye-like spots on its back and a flexible pointed snout. It spends the day buried in soft sand and comes out to hunt at dusk. Small shrimp and tiny fish will be eaten.
tips: Use fine sand so it can burrow without scraping its body.
A tight lid is essential; it escapes through small gaps.
Offer sinking foods in the evening.

items.name: Half-Banded Spiny Eel
items.temperament: Peaceful with fish too big to swallow
items.diet: Carnivore: live and frozen worms, shrimp, sinking foods
items.note: A burrowing, eel-like fish with a banded pattern and a pointed snout. It likes to hide in fine sand or caves and feeds at dusk. It will eat tiny fish and shrimp, and it can escape through very small openings.
tips: Provide fine sand and hiding places.
Cover every gap in the lid.
Feed sinking meaty foods after lights dim.

items.name: Norman's Lampeye
items.diet: Carnivore: micro pellets, baby brine shrimp, small frozen foods
items.note: A tiny, shimmering surface fish with a blue-green sheen and a bright eye. It is peaceful but small, so choose calm tankmates and give it a planted tank with floating plants.
tips: Keep a group of six or more.
Use floating plants and a lid with an air gap.
Offer tiny live or frozen foods.

items.name: Taiwan Moss
items.note: A fine-textured moss with arching, drooping strands. Tie or glue small pieces to wood or rock and trim them from time to time so it stays neat.
tips: Attach it to hardscape; do not bury it.
Keep it free of debris and algae.
Trim lightly to keep it dense.

items.name: Flame Moss
items.note: A moss that grows upward in flame-shaped tufts. It looks best attached on a piece of wood or rock where water moves gently over it.
tips: Attach with thread or glue; keep it out of the substrate.
Use gentle flow to keep dirt off the tufts.
Trim lightly to keep the flame shape.

items.name: Fissidens Moss
items.note: A small, feathery moss with flat, fern-like fronds that form neat tufts on hardscape. It grows slowly and likes clean water, so keep algae and debris off it.
tips: Attach to rock or wood and do not bury it.
Keep water clean and flow gentle.
Be patient; growth is slow.

items.name: Cyperus Helferi
items.note: A grass-like plant with long, flat leaves that sway in the current. It is easy to grow, spreads slowly, and works well as a background or side plant in moderate light.
tips: Plant in substrate with root tabs.
Trim older leaves to keep it tidy.
Give it room as it spreads.

items.name: Tonina Fluviatilis
items.note: A fine, upright stem plant with soft, narrow leaves. It likes strong light, CO2 and soft, slightly acidic water, and is not a plant for a first tank.
tips: Provide strong light, CO2 and regular fertilizer.
Keep water clean; it is sensitive to poor conditions.
Plant gently; stems are fragile.

items.name: Nomaphila
items.note: A large, broad-leaved stem plant that grows quickly and soaks up nutrients. It is best for the back of a tank that is at least two feet tall.
tips: Trim and replant the tops often.
Give it space; it can shade smaller plants.
Easy in most water, including hard water.

items.name: Golden Creeping Jenny
items.note: A pond-edge plant with round, golden-green leaves that is sold for aquariums and paludariums. It does best with its leaves above water; fully underwater it tends to weaken over time.
tips: Best grown emersed in a paludarium or at the water line.
Trim and replant healthy stems if grown underwater.
Never release it outdoors; it spreads aggressively.

items.name: Utricularia Graminifolia
items.note: A tiny carpeting plant with grass-like leaves that forms a dense lawn in strong light with CO2. It is a bladderwort, so it also has tiny traps. Plant in small tufts and be patient.
tips: Needs strong light and CO2 for a tight carpet.
Plant in small tufts; it can lift at first.
Keep the water clean to avoid algae.

items.name: Pogostemon Erectus
items.note: A fast-growing stem plant with narrow, whorled leaves that forms a bright green background. It does best in good light with CO2, and the top shoots can be trimmed and replanted.
tips: Trim and replant the tops often.
Give it nutrients, especially iron, for strong growth.
Plant in groups for a full background.

items.name: Weeping Moss
items.note: A drooping, easygoing moss that forms cascading strands once attached to driftwood or rock. It is a hardy choice for shrimp tanks and beginner aquascapes.
tips: Tie or glue to wood or rock; do not bury it.
Trim to keep it neat and to prevent debris buildup.
Keep the water clean to avoid algae.

items.name: Hygrophila Pinnatifida
items.note: A rhizome plant with crinkled, deeply lobed leaves, grown attached to driftwood or rock like a fern. It is slow growing and can brown if buried or kept in very soft water.
tips: Attach to wood or rock; do not bury the rhizome.
Keep light moderate to avoid algae on slow leaves.
Be patient; it grows slowly.

items.name: Glowlight Tetra
items.diet: Omnivore: micro pellets, flakes, small frozen foods
items.note: A small, calm tetra with a glowing gold-orange stripe along its body. It is hardy, shows its best color in a planted tank with subdued light, and mixes well with other small peaceful fish.
tips: Keep a group of six or more.
Dark substrate and floating plants bring out the glow.
Not the same as the glowlight danio or glowlight rasbora.

items.name: Mosquito Rasbora
items.diet: Micro pellets, crushed flakes, baby brine shrimp, microworms
items.note: A tiny red-orange nano fish, one of the smallest in the hobby. It does best in a quiet planted tank with gentle flow and only calm, small tankmates; larger fish will bully or eat it.
tips: Keep a group of eight or more.
Do not mix with fish that can swallow them.
Offer tiny foods; large pellets are too big.

items.name: Scissortail Rasbora
items.diet: Omnivore: flakes, small pellets, frozen foods
items.note: A slender, fast silver rasbora with a black and white scissor pattern on its tail fork. It is larger and more active than most rasboras, so it needs swimming room and a tight lid.
tips: Use a long tank and a tight lid; they jump.
Keep six or more.
Avoid tiny shrimp and tiny fish as tankmates.

items.name: Red Zebra Cichlid
items.diet: Mostly vegetable-based cichlid pellets and flakes; limited protein
items.note: A hardy Malawi mbuna. Males are blue and females orange, and the species is usually kept in a rock-heavy tank. It likes hard, alkaline water and can be pushy, so avoid crowding it with timid fish.
tips: Use plenty of rock caves and keep only one male per group.
Avoid high-protein foods that can cause bloat.
Keep it with other mbuna, not with soft-water fish.

items.name: Demasoni Cichlid
items.social: Large group of 10+ to spread aggression
items.diet: Mostly vegetable-based cichlid pellets and flakes; limited protein
items.note: A small blue and black striped mbuna from a tiny rocky area of Lake Malawi. It is feisty with its own kind, so it is normally kept in a large group in a rocky tank to share the aggression.
tips: Keep a big group; a few fish will fight.
Use lots of rockwork and sight breaks.
Do not mix with other blue-barred mbuna.

items.name: Kenyi Cichlid
items.diet: Mostly vegetable-based cichlid pellets and flakes; limited protein
items.note: Males turn bright yellow and females stay orange-blotched or blue-grey, and the species is a rowdy mbuna. Keep one male with several females in a tank with rocks and cave space, and do not expect it to get along with peaceful fish.
tips: Keep one male only unless the tank is large.
Provide rockwork and hiding places.
Feed a mostly plant-based diet.

items.name: Weather Loach
items.diet: Omnivore: sinking pellets, frozen and live worms
items.note: A long, eel-like loach that tolerates cooler water and lives for many years. It is active, likes to burrow, and grows larger than most people expect. Use soft sand and keep a small group.
tips: Use fine sand or smooth gravel so it can dig.
Keep a lid on the tank; it can escape.
Plan for 8 to 10 inches and many years.

items.name: Twig Catfish
items.level: Bottom to mid, clings to plants and wood
items.diet: Algae, biofilm and blanched vegetables; wood to graze
items.note: A very thin, stick-like catfish that blends in with plant stems and wood. It is gentle and slow but delicate, and it needs a mature tank with plenty of algae and biofilm to graze.
tips: Add it only to a mature tank.
Keep water clean and well oxygenated.
Offer blanched zucchini and algae wafers.

items.name: Croaking Gourami
items.diet: Carnivore-leaning omnivore: small frozen and live foods, micro pellets
items.note: A small gourami with a striped body. Males make a soft croaking sound when they display. It is calm but shy, and does best with gentle tankmates and floating plants.
tips: Leave an air gap above the water.
Use floating plants for cover.
Offer small meaty foods.

items.name: Threadfin Rainbowfish
items.diet: Micro pellets, baby brine shrimp, small frozen foods
items.note: A tiny rainbowfish whose males have long trailing fins. It is more delicate than other rainbowfish, so use calm tankmates and avoid fin nippers, strong flow and sudden water changes.
tips: Keep a group with extra females.
Provide gentle flow and plants.
Not a good match for fin nippers.

items.name: Red Rainbowfish
items.diet: Omnivore: flakes, small pellets, frozen foods
items.note: A deep-bodied rainbowfish in which males turn bright red as they mature. It is peaceful but active, likes hard, alkaline water, and needs a lid and a long tank. Young fish in the store often look plain.
tips: Keep more than six; males color up with company.
Prefers hard, alkaline water.
Use a long tank with open swimming space.

items.name: Sulawesi Cardinal Shrimp
items.diet: Biofilm, algae, shrimp pellets, blanched vegetables
items.note: A red and white shrimp from a warm, hard, alkaline lake. It needs warmer and harder water than common neocaridina or crystal shrimp, so do not use bee shrimp water recipes for it.
tips: Keep the water warm and hard.
Avoid copper-based medications.
Use rock and shell to supply minerals.

items.name: Mini Pellia
items.note: A flat, ribbon-like liverwort with small branching leaves. It grows slowly when attached to rock or wood and does best in clean water with gentle flow and low to moderate light.
tips: Attach with thread or glue and do not bury it.
Keep algae away with low light.
Do not expect fast growth.

items.name: Ranunculus Inundatus
items.note: A low carpeting plant with small bright green leaves and a delicate look. It wants strong light, CO2 and cooler water, and may struggle in a warm tropical tank.
tips: Plant in small tufts and keep the substrate nutrient rich.
Do not let it overheat.
Trim regularly to keep the carpet even.

items.name: Dwarf Water Lily
items.placement: Bulb or tuber in the substrate; leaves reach the surface
items.note: A bulb plant that sends up lily pads to the surface and sometimes flowers. Plant the bulb with the top exposed and trim the floating leaves if they shade other plants too much.
tips: Leave the top of the bulb above the substrate.
Trim floating leaves if they block light.
Give it a rich root-feeding substrate.

items.name: Lagenandra
items.note: A slow-growing crypt relative with broad, often reddish or brownish leaves. It does best left undisturbed in a rich substrate with moderate light, and it may melt briefly after planting.
tips: Do not disturb it once rooted.
Expect an adjustment period after planting.
Use root tabs in poor substrate.

items.name: Stargrass
items.note: A fast, bright green stem plant with narrow star-shaped leaves. It grows quickly with enough light and nutrients, and benefits from regular trimming and replanting of the tops.
tips: Trim and replant the tops to keep it bushy.
Needs good light and nutrients to stay full at the bottom.
Add iron-rich fertilizer if the leaves pale.

items.name: Pogostemon Stellatus
items.note: A leafy stem plant whose whorls of narrow leaves give it a full, feathery look. It prefers good light, steady nutrients and stable conditions, and it can grow tall and bushy with trimming.
tips: Give it good light and steady nutrients.
Trim the tops and replant them to keep it full.
Avoid moving it once it is rooted.

items.name: Pygmy Chain Sword
items.note: A grass-like foreground plant that spreads by runners into a lawn. It adapts to many tanks, and stronger light and fertilizer give a thicker carpet and redder new growth.
tips: Plant small clumps spaced a few inches apart.
Trim runners to keep it from spreading everywhere.
Use root tabs for a thicker carpet.

items.name: Pearl Weed
items.note: A bright green stem plant with small round leaves that forms a dense, bushy patch when trimmed. Under strong light it sprinkles the leaves with tiny oxygen bubbles, the effect that gives it its name.
tips: Plant it in small clumps and trim often.
Give it strong light and some fertilizer for dense growth.
It is not dwarf baby tears; the two are different plants.

items.name: Persicaria (Polygonum) Stem Plant
items.note: A hardy stem plant with narrow pointed leaves that can turn red-brown under strong light. It grows steadily, roots well, and tolerates a wide range of conditions if it gets light and nutrients.
tips: Trim and replant the tops to keep it bushy.
Stronger light brings out red tones.
Give it root tabs or a rich substrate.

items.name: Brazilian Micro Sword (Lilaeopsis)
items.note: A fine, grass-like carpet plant with thin bright green blades. It spreads by runners across the foreground and looks best under good light in a tank with a nutrient-rich substrate.
tips: Plant in small tufts, a little apart, so runners can fill in.
Needs good light and a nutrient-rich substrate to carpet.
Trim gently; very short trimming can slow it.

items.name: Cryptocoryne pontederiifolia
items.note: A sturdy crypt with long, heart-shaped, bubbly-edged leaves on tall stems. It is tougher than many crypts, doing well in low to medium light in a nutrient-rich substrate, and may drop leaves (melt) after a move before regrowing.
tips: Expect some melting when first planted; it regrows.
Use root tabs; it feeds through the roots.
Do not move it once settled.

items.name: Water Hedge (Didiplis diandra)
items.note: A fine-leaved stem plant with feathery, slender stems that tolerates cooler tanks than many tropical stem plants. Under strong light it turns reddish and makes a dense, soft-looking hedge.
tips: Plant bunches and trim tops to keep it bushy.
Strong light brings out red tones.
Handles cooler water, so it suits unheated room-temperature tanks.

items.name: Cryptocoryne Varieties
items.placement: Foreground to background, rosette, depends on species
items.note: Crypts such as undulata, spiralis, retrospiralis, crispatula, becketii, walkeri, petchii, nurii and usteriana share the same basic care: a nutrient-rich substrate with root tabs, steady conditions and patience. Size varies a lot by species, from compact 4-inch rosettes to leaves well over a foot long, so check the exact crypt before planting.
tips: Expect leaves to melt after planting or a change in conditions; they regrow from the roots.
Use root tabs; crypts feed through the roots.
Do not move them once settled.

items.name: Mexican Oak Leaf Plant
items.note: A tough stem plant with lobed, oak-like leaves. It tolerates cooler water and a wide range of conditions, so it works in unheated tanks as well as tropical ones, and its leaves are a soft green that can turn reddish in strong light.
tips: Trim the tops and replant the cuttings.
It grows quickly toward the surface and can shade lower plants.
Tolerates cooler temperatures than most stem plants.

items.name: Willow Moss
items.note: A dark green, feathery moss that grows best in cool water. It suits unheated tanks, ponds and coldwater tanks, and it can struggle or melt if the water stays warm for long.
tips: Prefers cool water; avoid long periods above the mid-70s F.
Tie or glue it to wood or rock.
Keep the water clean to prevent algae on the strands.

items.name: Orchid Plant (Barclaya)
items.note: A bulb plant related to water lilies with long, wavy, red-bronze to green leaves. It prefers warm, soft, clean water and a nutrient-rich substrate, and it can drop leaves after being moved before it recovers.
tips: Use root tabs; it feeds through the roots.
Do not move it once settled.
Prefers soft, warm water with steady conditions.

items.name: Selaginella (Spike Moss)
items.placement: Emersed in a paludarium or humid terrarium
items.note: A soft, fern-like moss relative that is sold alongside aquarium plants. It is not a true aquatic plant: it does best with its leaves in humid air above the water line and will not survive being fully submerged long term.
tips: Keep the leaves out of the water.
Provide constant humidity.
Good for paludariums and terrarium backgrounds.

items.name: Ranalisma Rostratum
items.note: A small rosette plant that spreads by runners into a low patch of ribbon-like leaves. It does best in bright light, nutrient-rich substrate and CO2 injection.
tips: Plant in nutrient-rich substrate.
Provide strong light and CO2.
Trim runners to control spread.

items.name: Littorella Uniflora
items.origin: Cool, soft waters of northern Europe and North America
items.note: A slow, grass-like carpet plant that prefers cooler, softer water than most tropical species. It can work in a tropical tank but often grows more slowly and may struggle in warm water.
tips: Prefers cooler, soft water.
Use fine substrate and strong light.
Be patient; growth is slow.

items.name: Red Stem Milfoil (Myriophyllum mattogrossense)
items.note: A fine-leaved stem plant with reddish tones under strong light. It grows quickly but collects debris in the feathery foliage, so keep it trimmed and the tank clean.
tips: Trim often to keep the foliage dense.
Keep water clean; fine leaves trap debris.
Strong light brings out the red color.

items.name: Hedyotis Salzmannii
items.note: A low, creeping plant with small oval leaves that spreads across the front of the tank. It prefers strong light and benefits from CO2 and a nutrient-rich substrate.
tips: Give strong light and CO2.
Trim stems to keep it compact.
Plant small bunches at the front.

items.name: Eriocaulon Cinereum
items.note: A small, grass-like rosette plant that is sold in tissue culture cups. It is slow and demanding, preferring soft, slightly acidic water, steady CO2 and a clean, mature tank.
tips: Use soft, slightly acidic water if possible.
Add steady CO2 and strong light.
Avoid algae-prone lighting; it is slow and easily smothered.

items.name: Vesuvius Sword
items.origin: Cultivated form of a South American plant
items.note: A sword-type plant with long, wavy, ribbon-like leaves that give a dramatic grassy effect. It is a cultivar of Bolivian sword, easy to grow, and spreads by runners.
tips: Plant in nutrient-rich substrate.
Trim older leaves to keep it tidy.
Give it room; it fills a corner quickly.

items.name: Giant Baby Tears
items.note: A bright green, small-leaved stem plant that forms a soft bush when planted in groups. It is bigger and easier than dwarf baby tears but still does best with good light, regular trimming and some fertilizer.
tips: Plant in small groups and trim the tops to bush out.
Strong light and CO2 give the densest growth.
Keep water clean; it melts if conditions swing.

items.name: Sagittaria Platyphylla
items.origin: Southern United States and the Caribbean
items.note: A grass-like plant with flat, ribbon-shaped leaves that spreads by runners. It is a different species from the dwarf sagittaria (Sagittaria subulata) but is used the same way: plant it in clumps in the foreground or midground and trim to keep it short.
tips: Plant the crown at the substrate surface, not buried.
Root tabs help it spread and stay healthy.
Trim tall leaves and thin runners to keep it tidy.
